notes.text:
The collection already has the nonspecific handle `rapa-britanico` (“Rapa — Londres”), but its source gives no accession or distinguishing description. This catalogue entry cannot be matched to that handle, and several selected BM dance-paddles could fit it. The catalogue labels this combined field “Found/Acquired”; it is retained as source wording and is not treated as an independently established findspot. A separate “Production place” field is represented as made_at when present.

30 September 2026 identity review: ambiguous crosswalk to `rapa-britanico`; keep this catalogue source unlinked. The British Museum identifies Museum number Oc,+.2600 (https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/E_Oc-2600), a Rapa dance-paddle, 81.60 × 19.70 × 2.20 cm, made of toromiro wood. The BM and independent 2022 [Art of the Ancestors curation](https://www.artoftheancestors.com/blog/rapa-nui-easter-island-british-museum) identify this accession, with Franks's 1885 donation; its description is an anthropomorphic carving with a repaired torso edge and terminal. The generic Arte row supplies only Rapa and Museo Britanico/Londres. Other candidates include Oc.5848 and Oc.5849, as well as Oc,+.2598 and Oc,+.2599 in the Franks/sailor acquisition group, so this distinctive object still cannot be assigned to the generic row. Resolution needs an image or primary description tied to that row, or a historical accession crosswalk.
